name: All That for a Hand Crack?
text: [approach] Parties camp on the level snow shelf beneath the west face, and the routes are spread along the foot of that face from camp.
[descent_text] After the second pitch, mantel above the anchor onto the snow, which leads to the descent line.
[descent_text] Walk off to the south over the snow, the same way as for the other routes on the west face.

name: Granitic Dreams
text: [overview] Length varies with snowpack: about 230 feet in June, with the first anchors near 140 feet, and at least 30-40 feet longer after summer melt.
[approach] Parties camp on the level snow shelf beneath the west face, and the routes are spread along the foot of that face from camp.
[descent_text] Walk off to the south over the snow, the same way as the other west face routes.
[descent_text] Rappelling this line is a poor idea because it is long, and snowmelt over the season lengthens it further.

name: Mt. Michelson - North Ridge
text: [overview] this line climbs the ridge on the north side, lying between the two northern glaciers.
[overview] Esetuk Creek is followed beyond many forks over wet tundra, then rock, talus and boulder slopes holding snow into June;
[overview] Cross Esetuk Glacier close to the toe, climb steeper boulders to the ridge, then mostly snow steepening to about 45 degrees.
[overview] Early-season snow may be loose, with deep postholing.
[detailed_rack] Pickets are possible later in the season, once the snow is consolidated.
[approach] The ground is wet tundra giving way to talus and boulder slopes where snow lingers into June, and the travel is slow and tedious.
[approach] Go over the Esetuk Glacier close to its terminus to get to the root of the peak, then work up a steep boulder field to a higher point on the ridge, where the terrain turns to snow.

name: Skunk
text: [overview] Climb 70-80 degree steps interspersed with gentler ramps for about 80 feet to the alders, then weave through them and tunnel up steep, sometimes deep snow, perhaps tying off alders for protection.

name: Dragonfly Jr.
text: [overview] P2: climb up and right to steeper sustained ice for 50 m until it eases, then 13 m of gentle ice and snow lead to a big ice chunk on the right, a comfortable belay spot.
[approach] Leave a vehicle at the plowed pullout beside the Parks Highway, on its west side, and ski or snowmachine up Cantwell Creek to the boundary of the Denali wilderness.
[approach] Snowmachines are left at the boundary;
[approach] The climb is on an east-northeast-facing wall, partly hidden by a spine coming off the rocky face south of the glacier.
[approach] Skirt the big snow bowl to reach the foot of the ice.
[approach] The Cantwell Glacier above can shed seracs onto the route, and rockfall potential is above average.

name: Didilkama Traverse
text: [overview] Beyond, descend toward the next tower and follow the ridge to the Snowbird Glacier, where route finding, rappels or hard downclimbing may be needed.

name: Northwest Couloir
text: [overview] A steep snow couloir;
[overview] ski or snowboard descents typically rappel to get in.
[detailed_rack] Steep snow in highly complex avalanche terrain;
[approach] The terrain is steep snow and very complex avalanche terrain, so check the local avalanche forecast first.

name: Rhinestone Wizard
text: [overview] climb it only when snowfall has been light or the hazard is low.
[overview] P4 (WI4/5): mushroomed pillar or curtain to a snow stance at the bottom of a big basin.
[overview] Afterward, cross snow toward the upper left to reach the ridge and walk west, or thread and reverse the approach.
[approach] The route is on the south face of Tiehacker Mountain, up Glacier Creek above Seward.
[descent_text] Descend by V-thread rappels, or climb snow up to the ridge on Tiehacker and follow the summer trail down to the Bear Lake neighborhood.

name: Goldfinger
text: [overview] good weather and dry conditions are hard to catch (snow near the summit, storms and water on pitch 3 turned parties back).
[overview] After lots of snowfall, start left of the main corner on easy ground to a ledge, after steep snow with a hidden moat (belay it).

name: South Gully/Ridge
text: [overview] A wide snow couloir at 40-50 degrees, bending slightly right, runs for 1800 feet before it constricts, forks and kicks up.
[overview] The right fork rises several hundred feet more and may hold some combination of ice, snow and rock, possibly with moderate ice or mixed climbing.
[overview] a brief snow traverse at low angle leads to the next couloir, which turns left onto the south ridge.
[overview] The ridge is easy 4th class with gendarme bypasses to a snowfield summit.
[overview] The couloir funnels debris, so move quickly and early and watch snow conditions.
[detailed_rack] Natural gear, slung horns and perhaps a picket or two.

name: Toe gully
text: [overview] Tools and crampons are optional.
[approach] Follow the first fault line up to the basin of the Cleveland Glacier, then continue up the basin to the obvious cliff band.
